slides.title: Assume every layer can fail
slides.text: Professionals never ask whether a layer is perfect. They assume any single layer can fail, and stack independent layers so one failure is never the whole story. That is defense in depth.
slides.alt: Lock It in Pro opens with the sharing sort: security starts with knowing what must be protected.

focus.cue: The sharing sort that opens Lock It in Pro
Share, or keep private: the first layer is a decision

slides.title: The personal layer stack
slides.text: For your own accounts the stack is short: updates, a unique passphrase per account, two-step sign-in, and backups. Each layer covers a failure the others cannot.
slides.alt: The Pro mailbox key builder: a passphrase made of chosen words, different from every other account key.

focus.cue: A unique passphrase per account starts here

slides.title: Each layer covers another
slides.text: A phished passphrase meets the second step and stops. A stolen tablet meets encryption and a backup, and the loss shrinks to hardware. Layers earn their keep on each other's worst days.
slides.alt: Share or Shield: your mailbox key. Anyone who has it can read your post and send as you, so it stays private.

focus.cue: The card about your mailbox key
Share or Shield: every fact has a good side and a risk

slides.title: Updates patch real holes
slides.text: Software ships with small flaws, and attackers collect the ones that get found. Updates are how those vulnerabilities get closed, which is why postponing them leaves a known door open.
slides.alt: The home router still has its key on a sticker anyone can read. Build a new passphrase from four word tiles.

focus.cue: The home router, with its key on a sticker
The sticker word itself, offered as a tile

slides.title: Audit a scenario account
slides.text: One account, four facts. Audit it against the stack and name the missing layer.
steps: Passphrase reused from another site: unique layer missing
No second step at sign-in: two-step layer missing
Photos exist nowhere else: backup layer missing
Updates postponed for months: patch layer missing
slides.alt: Physical or Digital: the sort whose bins are the machine and the data, from locked doors to firewalls.

focus.cue: A privacy screen on the monitor: physical or digital?

slides.title: Score your own setup
slides.text: Your layer audit needs no real account details: score the shape, not the secrets. Four layers present is a strong stack. Two is a plan for this week, written down.
slides.alt: The last Lock It sort in Pro: judging what is safe to do, the habit of naming a risk before you act.
